newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU panel rejects 30,000 T US malting barley quota.
newsitem.headline: EU panel rejects 30,000 T US malting barley quota.

text.p: A European Union trade committee rejected a proposal to open a 30,000-tonne reduced tariff quota for imports of U.S. malting barley, a European Commission spokesman said.
On December 4 the Commission proposed the quota, which would have been valid for the rest of 1996 and would have allowed the import of U.S. malting barley at 50 percent of the full duty.
"It's never happened before," said the spokesman, referring to the EU's so-called 113 committee of member state trade officials.
The committee rejected the proposal, saying the EU already had too much malting barley, Commission sources said.
The U.S. has complained about the EU's delay in opening the reduced tariff -- compensation to U.S. exporters for the loss of Austrian, Swedish and Finnish markets after they joined the EU in 1995.
Malting barley tariffs are one of a number of farm trade disputes, notably rice, being discussed by the EU and U.S.
U.S. officials, headed by Paul Drazek, trade adviser to U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, are in Brussels for negotiations on an agreement on the mutual recognition of veterinary standards.
